content.text:
Yes—**original Coca‑Cola did contain cocaine**, but not in the form people usually imagine.

When Coca‑Cola was created in **1886**, one of its ingredients was **extract of coca leaf**, the same plant cocaine is derived from. At the time, coca-based tonics and medicines were common and legal.

However:

- The amount of cocaine was relatively small.
- Coca‑Cola began reducing/removing cocaine around the early **1900s**.
- By about **1903**, the company had moved to using **“spent” coca leaves**, meaning leaves from which cocaine had been extracted.
- Modern Coca‑Cola **does not contain cocaine**.

Today, Coca‑Cola reportedly still uses a coca-leaf flavoring extract, but the cocaine alkaloid is removed under tightly regulated processing.
